sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's domestic digital economy (e-commerce, fintech, media) is decoupling from US tech weakness, driven by rising middle-class consumption and government digitalization push.
Local tech listings (BELI, IRSX, WGSH) are outperforming due to scarce float and retail participation, creating durable liquidity-driven premiums.
US-listed tech names in the Indonesian portfolio (HPQ, CYBR) face structural headwinds from higher-for-longer rates and AI capex digestion, warranting underweight.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names on local resilience, but stay defensive on US-exposed subsectors. BELI and IRSX momentum signals strong domestic demand; add BUKA on e-commerce recovery. Trim US-linked positions (HPQ, CYBR) given -2.21% drag. Watch WGSH for continued upside. Overall, maintain WATCH, not overweight, until US tech stabilizes.

Structural under-penetration of insurance and multi-finance in Indonesia supports sustained earnings growth for LIFE, AHAP, and BFIN, independent of global macro swings.
Regulatory tailwinds for sharia-compliant and micro-lending products are creating durable niches, lifting BGTG, BBLD, and TRJA as domestic liquidity rotates into specialized lenders.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to Indonesian financials, led by BSIM and LIFE, as domestic catalysts (rate cuts, loan growth) outweigh US weakness. Favor small-cap insurers and multi-finance names with strong momentum; trim US-sensitive banks. Position for continued ID outperformance over 1-2 months, targeting +5-8% upside on leaders.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export volumes remain structurally supported by Asian thermal demand, especially from China and India, sustaining earnings visibility for large-cap producers like BUMI.
Nickel downstreaming policy, including domestic processing mandates and export bans on raw ore, continues to drive value-add margins for integrated players such as CUAN and FIRE.
The IDX's relative outperformance over US equities signals persistent local investor appetite for energy assets, supported by government infrastructure spending and energy security programs.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum in coal and nickel-linked names (BUMI, CUAN, FIRE) on near-term export demand and IDX strength, but avoid chasing speculative small caps (SQMI, ALKA) given WATCH signal and US flatness. Rotate into producers with confirmed volume guidance and hedge against rupiah volatility.

Pricing power and distribution reach separate winners from laggards, favoring companies with strong brand equity and rural penetration.
US-linked FMCG underperformance signals a structural shift toward local champions, as investors prioritize domestic demand over export-oriented plays.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in high-momentum names (KKES, COCO, ENZO) as local consumer demand stays resilient, but trim exposure to US-linked FMCG laggards. Focus on domestic staples with strong distribution and pricing power; expect continued rotation into small/mid-cap winners. Maintain normal risk, add on dips.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's universal health coverage (JKN) expansion continues to drive volume growth for hospital chains and pharmaceutical distributors, insulating them from global macro swings.
Domestic healthcare names benefit from a young, growing middle class with rising out-of-pocket spending on private care, a durable tailwind absent in mature US markets.
Regulatory support for local vaccine and generic drug manufacturing (e.g., NOVN, DKHH) is accelerating import substitution, creating structural margin expansion opportunities.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian hospital operators (HEAL, SAME) and pharma distributors (DKHH) as domestic healthcare demand outpaces US peers; AIMS' +25% spike is speculative—take profits. Rotate into NOVN for vaccine upside. Maintain neutral US exposure; MRNA/CVS rallies are sentiment-driven, not structural.
